step1_analysis.circuit_type: Fully differential capacitive feedback amplifier / Integrator
step1_analysis.description: This circuit is a fully differential capacitive feedback amplifier, likely serving as a discrete-time integrator or a multiplying digital-to-analog converter (MDAC) stage in a sigma-delta modulator. It uses an operational amplifier with input and feedback capacitors to set the closed-loop gain and perform charge transfer.

paper_reference.title: A 2.5-V Sigma–Delta Modulator for Broadband Communications Applications

closed_loop_gain.description: Closed-loop AC gain of the amplifier stage

sky130_expected.reasoning: The closed-loop gain is strictly determined by the ratio of the input sampling capacitors (C3, C4) to the feedback capacitors (C1, C2).
Depends on the core op-amp's gain-bandwidth product and the capacitive feedback factor (beta). Modeled here to match the paper's ~4 MHz target.

opamp_open_loop_gain.description: Open-loop DC gain of the core operational amplifier

sky130_expected.calculation: gm * ro of the cascoded op-amp stages
sky130_expected.reasoning: High open-loop gain is required to minimize leakage and harmonic distortion in the sigma-delta modulator integrator.

power_consumption.description: Total power consumption of the block

sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports 150 mW for the entire broadband modulator. A single integrator op-amp in SKY130 would likely consume 1-10 mW depending on slew rate requirements.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure the closed-loop AC gain, bandwidth, and transient step response of the capacitive feedback amplifier.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Capacitive Feedback Amplifier Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Parameterized capacitor values
.param C_f = 1p
.param C_s = 2p
.param C_L = 0.5p
.param C_p = 0.1p

* Ideal fully differential amplifier subcircuit (Macro-model)
* Modeled for ~96dB open-loop gain and ~10MHz GBW with 0.5pF load
.subckt amplifier out_p cm out_n in_m in_p
  G1 out_p cm in_m cm 31.4u
  R1 out_p cm 2G
  G2 out_n cm in_p cm 31.4u
  R2 out_n cm 2G
.ends

* DUT (Modified A1 to X1 for subcircuit call, added capacitor values)
X1 Vout_p LABEL_NET_0 Vout_n N3 N2 amplifier
C1 Vout_n N2 {C_f}
C2 Vout_p N3 {C_f}
C3 N3 Vstep_p {C_s}
C4 N2 Vstep_n {C_s}
C5 Vout_n GND {C_L}
C6 N2 GND {C_p}
C7 Vout_p GND {C_L}
C8 N3 GND {C_p}

* DC feedback resistors to establish operating point (1 Gohm)
R_fb1 Vout_n N2 1G
R_fb2 Vout_p N3 1G

* Bias and Stimulus
VLABEL_NET_0 LABEL_NET_0 0 0.9
Vstep_p Vstep_p LABEL_NET_0 dc 0 ac 1 pulse(0 0.1 10n 1n 1n 1u 2u)
Vstep_n Vstep_n LABEL_NET_0 dc 0 ac -1 pulse(0 -0.1 10n 1n 1n 1u 2u)

* Dummy VDD for power measurement reference
Vdd vdd 0 1.8
Rdummy vdd 0 1k

* Differential measurement helpers
E_out_diff out_diff 0 Vout_p Vout_n 1
E_in_diff in_diff 0 Vstep_p Vstep_n 1

.control
  * DC Operating Point
  op
  print v(Vout_p) v(Vout_n) v(N3) v(N2)
  let power = -i(Vdd) * 1.8
  print power

  * AC Analysis for Closed-Loop Gain and Bandwidth
  ac dec 100 100 100Meg
  let gain_db = vdb(out_diff) - vdb(in_diff)
  meas ac midband_gain_db find gain_db at=10k
  meas ac bw_3db when gain_db=(midband_gain_db - 3) fall=1

  * Transient Analysis for Step Response
  tran 1n 2u
  meas tran vout_step_min min v(out_diff)
  meas tran vout_step_max max v(out_diff)
  
  quit
.endc
.end
